holidays.name: National Memo Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble office memo. Write a pointed, passive-aggressive, or heartfelt memo to a coworker, or simply appreciate the art of the brief written note.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance tied to workplace culture and the history of internal business communication. Its exact founder is unclear, as with many quirky calendar days.
holidays.funFact: The word 'memo' is short for 'memorandum,' Latin for 'something to be remembered.'

holidays.name: National Strawberries and Cream Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in the classic pairing of juicy strawberries and fluffy whipped or heavy cream. Perfect for dessert, breakfast, or a sunny afternoon snack.
holidays.origin: A food observance that coincides with the start of strawberry season in many regions. The pairing became famous at the Wimbledon tennis championships, where it has been a tradition since the 1870s.
holidays.funFact: Wimbledon spectators eat roughly 190,000 portions of strawberries and cream during the tournament.

holidays.name: World Day for Cultural Diversity for Dialogue and Development
holidays.description: A United Nations observance celebrating the richness of the world's cultures and encouraging people to learn about and engage with different traditions, languages, and perspectives.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly established it in 2002 after UNESCO's Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity, adopted in 2001.
holidays.funFact: There are over 7,000 languages spoken in the world today, but nearly half are at risk of disappearing.

holidays.name: I Need a Patch for That Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for crafters, scouts, and jacket-decorators to celebrate patches of all kinds, whether embroidered, iron-on, or sew-on, and to find one for every hobby, joke, or personality quirk.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted unofficial observance among the crafting and patch-collecting communities, fueled by the rise of patch culture on denim jackets and backpacks.
holidays.funFact: Embroidered patches date back to ancient times, when they were used to mark military units, and they remain a staple of uniforms today.

holidays.name: Talk Like Yoda Day
holidays.description: Fans of Star Wars speak in Yoda's famously inverted syntax. Quote the Jedi Master, you must. Fun, it will be.
holidays.origin: A pop culture observance linked to the release of Star Wars: Episode III, Revenge of the Sith on May 19, 2005, and the broader Star Wars celebration season in May.
holidays.funFact: Yoda's speech pattern is called object-subject-verb order, which is very rare in natural human languages.
